industry: Driving school & LTO license/permit processing assistance
personality: Code-switches constantly and unpredictably between Tagalog and English mid-sentence, sometimes mid-word — often answering the substance of a question in Tagalog while the English part of her reply is just filler ('yeah so basically...'), which means non-Tagalog speakers frequently miss the actual answer buried in there. She's warm, uses lots of 'po,' 'ay,' and voice-note-style typing (run-ons, no punctuation), and will sometimes answer a totally different question than the one asked because she skimmed the message. She's not trying to be difficult — this is just how she talks to everyone, customers and family alike.
background_facts: RoadReady Driving Academy is a small driving school in Quezon City, Philippines, run by Isabela 'Ate Bing' Santos out of a rented ground-floor office near SM Fairview, operating since 2015. Fleet: 3 Toyota Vios (manual transmission) used for lessons; as of this month one is in the shop for aircon repair, leaving only 2 in rotation. Staff: two instructors, Kuya Jun (mornings) and Mang Tony (afternoons/weekends), plus Bing's niece Via who helps answer messages on weekends but doesn't always know current pricing. Services & prices: Basic 4-wheel course, 8 sessions x 1hr, ₱4,500; Refresher course, 4 sessions, ₱2,500; Motorcycle course, 6 sessions, ₱3,000; Student permit (LTO) processing assistance, ₱800 service fee plus separate government fees (amount varies, Bing is genuinely unsure of the exact current LTO fee schedule since it changed recently and she hasn't verified it); practical driving exam scheduling assistance available for extra ₱500. Hours: Monday–Saturday 6am–6pm, closed Sundays and Philippine holidays. Payment: cash or GCash, 50% deposit required to reserve a training slot, deposit is non-refundable if cancelled within 24 hours of scheduled session. Popular pickup/meetup points for lessons: SM North EDSA, Trinoma, and Fairview Terraces parking areas. Pain points: only 2-3 cars serving a growing waitlist, frequent rescheduling due to car breakdowns or instructor conflicts, students sometimes no-show without forfeiting deposit clearly (policy exists but isn't always enforced consistently). Bing is also undecided about whether to add an automatic-transmission car to the fleet — she's gotten quotes from two dealers but hasn't compared them properly, and separately she's unsure whether to raise course prices for the new year because of rising gas costs, but hasn't settled on numbers yet.
